html: Baratza says Single Dose auto-stop and Timer Mode both work with either the single-dose lid or the shut-off hopper. The lid does not lock the owner into one routine. For changing beans, pre-weigh each dose and verify output; for one house coffee, time a few doses and check mass when beans change. Neither mode weighs coffee. Checked October 15, 2026. [source]
note: US Encore ESP Pro listing states both dosing modes are compatible with the included single-dose lid and shut-off hopper.

html: The current Flair 58 Plus 2 manual treats its integrated preheat system as an electrical assembly during cleanup: switch it off, let the brew head cool, keep the outside and wiring dry, and wipe the inside and plunger with a damp cloth. A cooler-water flush can follow for heavier residue, but the heated brew head must not be immersed. This differs from rinsing a fully detached, unheated Flair cylinder at the sink. Checked October 15, 2026. [source]
note: Plus 2 manual cleaning panel: switch off and cool; damp-cloth interior/plunger cleaning, optional cool-water flush, never immerse heated brew head.

html: Flair's Classic support guide calls preheating the stainless brew cylinder part of the brew, not an optional upgrade. Its fill-and-dump method leaves boiling water in the inverted cylinder for about 30 seconds and recommends repeating the cycle before assembling the shot. That adds active handling to each cold start; the same guide says a still-warm cylinder may not need another preheat between back-to-back extractions. Budget this time when comparing Classic with an electrically heated Flair 58. Checked October 15, 2026. [source]
note: Classic support article specifies fill/dump preheat, about 30 seconds and repeated cycles, with warm back-to-back cylinder caveat.

html: The NEO Flex's Flow Control portafilter needs a generation check at cleanup. Flair says the Flow Control 2 has a removable spout: separate and rinse spout and basket after a session, then let both dry upside down. An original fixed-spout Flow Control portafilter instead gets a cool water-only shot to flush residue. A used NEO Flex with an unverified basket should be identified before following either procedure; a blocked spout changes the pressure behavior the beginner basket is meant to simplify. Checked October 15, 2026. [source]
note: Flair support distinguishes Flow Control 2 removable-spout rinse from original fixed-spout water-only flush.

html: Flair's PRO 2 care guidance singles out the copper portafilter holder: wipe coffee residue from it after each use because the acidic residue can damage the finish. The removable plunger is a different task: rinse and dry it when needed, then use only a light application of food-safe oil on its O-rings if travel needs restoring. This routine is more specific than putting the whole detached brew head through a wash after every shot. Checked October 15, 2026. [source]
note: PRO 2 support article warns about acidic residue on copper holder and recommends occasional plunger cleaning with light food-safe O-ring lubrication.

html: Ascaso USA's current Steel DUO PID support page calls for a group screen and gasket replacement every six months as preventive maintenance, alongside weekly group and steam-tip cleaning for a two-to-three-drink home routine. Treat those as the distributor's service guidance, not a measured failure interval. Confirm the delivered US V3's parts and current manual with the seller before ordering seals or applying an older Duo procedure. The replacement schedule belongs in the ownership budget even if the machine still pulls shots normally. Checked October 15, 2026. [source]
note: Ascaso USA support FAQ calls for six-month screen/gasket preventive replacement and weekly cleaning at two to three drinks daily; revision-specific fit must be confirmed.
